expectation: Nuclear FOXP3 in regulatory T cells, a subset of CD4+ T cells. Uncommon: scattered single nuclei in the stroma, enriched in lymphoid aggregates and immune-dense areas. Expect a few dozen to hundreds of round nuclear dots with no tissue-wide signal.
observed: A: haze over the tissue, tiling, and bright dots both on and off the tissue. B/C: diffuse haze with a few large blobs, no nuclear dots. D: uniform haze. E: small grain and one blob in the CD4-dense field; in the merge, few green spots and they are not nuclear-sized dots on magenta cells.
why: There are no nuclear dots in a subset of CD4+ cells at any scale. The signal is haze, tiling, grain and debris blobs, some of them lying off the tissue.
notes: FOXP3 shows tissue haze, tile artefacts and bright debris spots, some outside the tissue. Even in the CD4-dense field it gives only fine grain and a stray blob. It does not mark nuclei within the CD4+ cells.
